brief: A small display stand: three bases meeting at a corner with a raised platform on a spike at that corner.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Three hex bases meeting at a shared corner/junction
requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full arranged in L-shape; all three touch at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 where spike is seated

requirements.requirement: Raised platform at that corner on a spike
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 mount-variant spike at the shared junction fitted with platform-lrg accessory (22.95x26.5mm small platform upgraded to 51.9x60mm large platform for display use, trapped on mount spike above the base tops)

Build is 3 bases only (no extra levels or extensions), 12 end caps + 3 joint bolts via house rules; platform centered over the junction provides a flat working surface belonging to no single cell for display

finish.summary: Built L-shaped cluster of three full hex bases sharing the corner junction at 0,0|0,1|1,0. Installed mount spike at that junction and fitted the large platform (platform-lrg) to create the raised display surface. Capped open faces and bolted joints for a finished stand.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
